details.body: Fix inconsistent SUB_ADULT_FEEDING_WEIGHT constant: 0.65 in crates/tank_core/src/types/biology.rs:148 vs 0.67 in crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:16. These two private constants serve the same conceptual role (sub-adult feeding demand relative to adults) but disagree on the value. biology.rs uses it in AnimalState::feeding_units() and add_reserve_by_feeding_units(), while shrimp.rs uses it in the actual daily feeding/routing/condition code. Consolidate to a single shared constant (or single source of truth) to prevent silent divergence in feeding weight calculations between the two modules.

Fix failing test trim_plants_is_closed_system_via_helpers in crates/tank_core/tests/budget_helpers.rs:242-267. Two issues: (1) Line 253 calls assert_n_conserved() but TrimPlantsAndRemove intentionally exports biomass from the tank — this is no longer a closed-system operation, so the nitrogen conservation assertion is incorrect for the renamed action semantics. (2) Line 259 looks up budget label "action:trim_plants" but the action was renamed to TrimPlantsAndRemove with budget label "action:trim_plants_and_remove" (engine.rs:791), so the lookup always returns None and the test would panic at the .expect() even if the conservation check passed.

Fix incorrect reserve fraction in RemoveShrimp action at crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:684. The code computes `removed_frac = count.min(total) / total` where `total = state.animal.total_count()` (adults + sub-adults + juveniles) but `count` is the number of adults to remove. This dilutes the reserve fraction — removing 5 adults from a population of 5 adults + 10 juveniles only removes 5/15 = 33% of adult reserve instead of 100%. The denominator should be `state.animal.adult.count` to correctly export the proportional adult reserve.

Remove dead code in crates/tank_core/src/types/biology.rs: the methods feeding_units() (line 441), add_reserve_by_feeding_units() (line 477), try_spend_reserve_g() (line 497), and transfer_dead_reserve_g() (line 517) have zero call sites across the entire codebase. They were likely intended as refactoring targets but the shrimp.rs code does the same operations inline with its own (different) constant values. Either wire these methods into the actual simulation code or remove them to avoid confusion with the divergent constants.

`/home/master/p/tank-simulation/crates/tank_core/tests/budget_tracking.rs:287`, `/home/master/p/tank-simulation/crates/tank_core/tests/budget_tracking.rs:303`, and `/home/master/p/tank-simulation/crates/tank_core/tests/budget_tracking.rs:441` hard-code the current animal cohort names (`adult`, `sub_adult`, `juvenile`) and only treat flat `animal.*_count` names as future fields. A new nested cohort following the current schema, such as `animal.larvae.count` or `animal.larvae.reserve_g`, would no longer be auto-discovered by the structural coverage test, so the budget component arrays could drift out of sync without this guard failing.

In check_param_range (provenance.rs:116-127), NaN values silently pass the range check because IEEE 754 comparisons with NaN always return false. Add a !value.is_finite() guard that produces a RangeWarning (or a distinct diagnostic) when the value is NaN or infinity, and add a test for this edge case.

The preset-level Provenance struct (presets.rs:14-19) uses confidence: Option<String>, allowing arbitrary strings like 'medium' (present in shipped TOML files default.toml:99 and soft_acidic.toml:23). The per-parameter ParamMeta uses the validated ConfidenceLevel enum. Either: (a) change Provenance.confidence to Option<ConfidenceLevel> and update the shipped TOML files to use valid enum values, or (b) document the intentional difference and add a note explaining that preset-level confidence is freeform while per-parameter confidence is validated.

Add validation that valid_range[0] <= valid_range[1] during deserialization or in check_param_range. An inverted range like [5.0, 0.1] would cause every value to trigger a spurious warning. A simple assertion or early return with a descriptive warning would prevent silent misconfiguration.

Normalize provenance display/range-check values for legacy total-style process parameters before feeding them to `format_param()` / `check_ranges()` (`crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:400-509`, `crates/tank_core/src/types/provenance.rs:148-158`). Several of the parameters being documented are explicitly stored in legacy total units and converted by the runtime to concentration units (`crates/tank_core/src/types/process.rs:56-63`, `crates/tank_core/src/types/process.rs:72-109`, `crates/tank_core/src/systems/nitrogen_cycle.rs:169-174`). Right now a value like `aob_k_tan_mg = 0.5` is displayed and range-checked as `0.5 mg N/L`, even though the engine actually uses `0.025 mg N/L`, so the new provenance output and `valid_range` diagnostics are scientifically wrong for these fields.

Add a provenance path for the active code-defined process defaults that are still hardcoded during scenario materialization. `ProcessParams` includes `death_biomass_to_detritus_fraction` and the microfauna routing fractions (`crates/tank_core/src/types/process.rs:211-247`), but `ProcessParamsPreset` has no fields/`param_meta` support for them and rejects unknown metadata keys (`crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:351-388`, `crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:392-500`, `crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:723-731`). `process_preset_to_params()` then injects literal values for them (`crates/tank_scenarios/src/lib.rs:433-443`) and drops provenance entirely. Those runtime parameters still cannot carry source/confidence/range metadata.

Fix failing test `step_hours_leaves_state_untouched_when_clamps_precede_a_validation_error` in `crates/tank_core/tests/validation.rs:141`. The engine mutates `habitat_registry` light_exposure values (roughly doubles them) during pre-step processing before the invariant validation error fires, so the state snapshot after the failed step does not match the expected clone. Either the engine must defer habitat-registry light updates until after invariant checks pass, or the test must account for the mutation.

Add `respiration_dic_rate_mg_c_per_g_per_hour` and `photosynthesis_dic_rate_mg_c_per_g_per_hour` to the non-negative/finite validation array in `ProcessParamsPreset::validate()` (`crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs`, around line 871). These two fields are present in the struct (line 242-243) and in `param_value()` (lines 433-437) but are absent from the validation fields list, meaning a TOML file setting them to NaN or negative values would silently pass validation.

Document in `ParamMeta.valid_range` (in `crates/tank_core/src/types/provenance.rs:57`) that for legacy `_mg` and `_mg_total` fields, valid_range values must be expressed in normalized concentration units (matching the `unit` field, e.g. mg/L), not in raw storage units. The `check_ranges()` path normalizes the VALUE via `provenance_value()` but does NOT normalize the range bounds, so TOML authors who write valid_range in raw units will get spurious or missing warnings.

Surface `valid_range` diagnostics from the normal process-parameter loader. `load_process_params()` only deserializes and runs `validate()` ([crates/tank_data/src/lib.rs:65-74]), while the new warning path lives in `ProcessParamsPreset::check_ranges()` ([crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:662-667]) and is never called there. In practice, an out-of-range or malformed `valid_range` loads silently in production, so the acceptance criterion for an explicit warning/diagnostic path is not actually met.

Extend the adjacent per-parameter metadata slot beyond `ProcessParamsPreset`. The new schema is only attached to process coefficients ([crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:503-508]); `SourceWaterPreset` still exposes only file-level `provenance` ([crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:29-49]) and `ShrimpPreset` does the same ([crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:142-185]). That means the task still cannot carry per-parameter source/confidence/range metadata for source-water chemistry or shrimp-life-history parameters without another schema/API change, which falls short of the requested chemistry-and-biology coverage.

PlantPreset and SubstratePreset do not implement param_meta support. The acceptance criteria states the schema should be 'flexible enough for both chemistry and biology parameters.' The ParamMeta schema itself is flexible, but plant parameters like growth_rate_index and water_column_uptake_bias — which are biology-relevant scientific parameters — cannot carry provenance at the preset level. Consider adding param_meta to PlantPreset (at minimum) for consistency, since the next bead (tanksim-6e5.7.2: 'Attach provenance to high-value chemistry and ecology parameters') will need to annotate plant params.

The acceptance criteria requires 'Decide how provenance is stored for code-defined defaults versus data-file parameters.' The implementation correctly uses TOML-level provenance for data-file params, and ProcessParams::Default has no inline provenance. However, this design decision is not documented anywhere — there is no comment in provenance.rs, process.rs, or the TOML files explicitly stating that code-defined defaults inherit provenance only when loaded through a TOML preset file, and that ProcessParams::Default values constructed without TOML have no provenance path. Add a brief design note (e.g., in provenance.rs or ROUTING.md) so downstream contributors understand the provenance boundary.

Update the shrimp provenance path so omitted optional fields fall back to the runtime defaults before formatting and range checks. Today `ShrimpPreset::lookup_param_value` returns `None` for optional fields such as `body_*`, `juvenile_to_subadult_days`, `base_clutch_size`, and `min_clutch_condition` when the TOML omits them (`crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:304-317`, `crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:476-502`), but `shrimp_preset_to_params` later injects real defaults from `ShrimpRuntimeParams::default()` (`crates/tank_scenarios/src/lib.rs:550-597`). That makes provenance on code-defined shrimp defaults effectively write-only: `format_param()` and `check_ranges()` never surface it even though the runtime uses a concrete value.

Make the new process-parameter formatter stop renormalizing legacy `_mg` / `_mg_total` values unless it can also show the corresponding metadata/unit, or automatically attach that derived unit. `ParamMetaPreset::format_param` currently calls `provenance_param_value()` before it checks whether any `param_meta` exists (`crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:59-64`), and `ProcessParamsPreset::provenance_param_value` always rewrites legacy compatibility fields into reference-tank concentrations (`crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:1144-1150`). Because the shipped default process preset intentionally has no `param_meta` (`crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:1857-1864`) but still stores `aob_k_tan_mg = 0.5` (`crates/tank_data/data/process/default.toml:31`), the debug helper can print a transformed value like `0.025` with no unit/source context, which is misleading.

Tighten `ProcessParamsPreset::validate` to reject `shrimp_juvenile_maturation_days <= 0`. The validator only rejects negative values today (`crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:1334-1387`), but scenario materialization immediately splits that legacy total into stage durations (`crates/tank_scenarios/src/lib.rs:546-564`; `crates/tank_core/src/types/biology.rs:342-354`) and runtime invariants require both resulting fields to be strictly positive (`crates/tank_core/src/invariants.rs:316-323`). A custom process preset with `shrimp_juvenile_maturation_days = 0.0` will therefore load successfully and only fail later when the engine is stepped.

Restore a real migration path for legacy kinetic `_mg` process keys instead of treating them as raw mg/L aliases. The runtime/data structs now only add `serde(alias = "..._mg")` for `decomposer_*`, `aob_*`, `nob_*`, and `comammox_*` in `crates/tank_core/src/types/process.rs:59-111` and `crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:763-801`, while `parse_process_params_preset()` only renormalizes the plant/algae `*_mg_total` keys in `crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:1186-1291`. `legacy_process_param_normalization()` no longer returns `LegacyMgPerL` for any renamed kinetic parameter in `crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs:1345-1365`, so a legacy file such as `aob_k_tan_mg = 0.5` is now interpreted as `0.5 mg N/L` instead of the previous `0.025 mg N/L`. The still-stale regression in `crates/tank_data/src/lib.rs:316-335` expecting `aob_k_tan_mg = 200.0` to report `value 10` shows the old 20 L compatibility contract was intended to remain intact.
